thread:
harper: Heads-up — ran into a weird SSE parsing edge in the mobile sample-app flow. When auth refresh + reconnect happen close together, the client sometimes ends up with a partial JSON token at the end of an event, then the next chunk starts with the rest of the token but our reassembly treats them as two separate 'data:' events and we try to parse the partial piece. Repro steps below.

leo: Which SDKs? Mobile wrapper or plain browser/node?

harper: This is the React Native (mobile) sample that wraps the node-sdk streaming client (we use fetch stream polyfill). Versions: mobile-sample v0.4.2, node-sdk v0.11.3. Happened on iOS simulator and an Android device.

harper: Repro (approx):
1) Start a long stream (server sends multiple `data:` events)
2) Force token expiry and trigger auth refresh while the stream is mid-flight (we saw this in flaky CI with short-lived dev creds)
3) Client reconnects quickly (we do immediate retry) and the rebuilt buffer sometimes contains a trailing fragment like `...\"text\":\"hello` (no closing quote/brace) then next chunk starts ` world\"}`

 so naive event join yields two data events: the first with incomplete JSON, second with remainder.

harper: Example capture (tcpdump-like, simplified):

```
data: {"id":1,"text":"hello
```

...then next chunk after reconnected socket:

```
 world"}
```

harper: Our current client handler splits on `\n\n` and then does `lines.filter(...).map(...).join('')` which joins the fragments and sometimes leaves the partial object isolated and attempted to parse alone because the split boundary fell between the chunks incorrectly.

ash: Can you paste the parsing code from the mobile wrapper?

harper: Sure (simplified):
```js
let acc = '';
res.on('data', c => {
  acc += c.toString();
  const evs = acc.split('\n\n');
  acc = evs.pop() || '';
  for (const e of evs) {
    const data = e.split('\n').filter(l => l.startsWith('data:')).map(l => l.slice(5)).join('');
    try { onEvent(JSON.parse(data)); } catch (err) { console.warn('partial-parse', data); }
  }
});
```

ash: Two issues: 1) join('') removes delimiters that can indicate empty/heartbeat events and will hide where fragments were. 2) Immediate reconnect after auth refresh means chunk boundaries align differently; a partial token can end up as its own event if there was an intervening empty data event or keepalive.

leo: Mobile fetch polyfills sometimes give chunked strings differently (UTF-8 split at surrogate pairs etc). We should be resilient to partial UTF-8 and partial JSON tokens.

harper: My quick local fix was to join with `\n` and treat whitespace-only assemblies as heartbeat, plus add a tiny backoff before reconnect to allow the server to close the prior stream cleanly. Patch I tried:
```js
const payload = e.split('\n').filter(l => l.startsWith('data:')).map(l=>l.slice(5)).join('\n');
if (!payload.trim()) continue; // heartbeat
try { onEvent(JSON.parse(payload)); } catch (err) { // push back into acc for next chunk
  acc = payload + acc; break; // wait for next chunk
}
```

harper: That avoided the crash in my runs but felt messy.

ash: I don't love mutating `acc` from inside the loop. Better to keep a small state machine: accumulate until a full JSON parse succeeds or reach explicit event boundary. Also canonicalize CRLF->LF and normalize surrogate pair handling.

leo: Action items proposal:
- harper: open GH issue + attach minimal repro (tcpdump + sample app script that forces auth refresh during stream)
- ash: implement canonical parseEventStream util that is stateful (accumulate lines, join with `\n`, treat empty data as heartbeat, requeue incomplete event until next chunk, normalize CRLF) and export to mobile/node/browser SDKs for parity
- leo: add small reconnect backoff in mobile sample as a bandaid and add a test in sdk-stream-fuzz to simulate auth-refresh/reconnect races and UTF-8 split points

replay-bot: CI queued for harper/sse-partial-json (tests: sdk-stream-fuzz)

harper: Filing issue now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/node-sdk/issues/811 (WIP). Will include the capture and a tiny repro harness. Thanks all :pray:

leo: Great, if you can include a small fuzz that splits at random byte offsets (including inside multibyte utf8 chars) that'll help catch more of these mobile-edge cases.

ash: Also add a short note in SDK parity doc about expected keepalive semantics and reconnect timing recommendations for sample apps.

harper: On it — patch incoming tomorrow.
